relevance_note: A 1975 pathology study and review of all 17 then-known patients with Tangier disease ("various tissues from 5 patients with Tangier disease"), with individual case reports; it predates gene identification and reports no ABCA1 variant.
method_note: Read the OCR-converted full text (heavily garbled in places). Tables 1 and 2 (clinical and histopathologic findings in 17 patients) are unreadable OCR noise, so nothing was taken from them; all per-patient values come from the case reports and from Discussion sentences that name patients by number. A Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON from hand-written values and spans and checked every span verbatim. No ABCA1 gene or variant is mentioned (pre-molecular era), so the variants table is empty and publications.n_patients_reported is null (no patient with an ABCA1 variant is stated); 17 patients with Tangier disease are summarized. Scope: all 17 numbered patients (each has at least one individual-level fact in the text) plus relatives described in relation to them: mother and father of patient 2 (bone marrow examined), father of patient 16 (PJa), and the two parents of patient 13 (sex not given). Patient numbers are the paper's labels ('patient N'). Patients 2, 4, 5, 15 and 16 are described first-hand, so source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' for them although 2 and 5 cite earlier reports (recorded in publications); patient 1 gets '2,3', patient 17 gets '14' (personal communication), patient 12 gets 'Kocen et al'. The sentence 'The latter patient 12 apparently incurred cerebral trauma at birth ... died of bronchopneumonia at 5% years of age' follows a sentence about patient 13 and matches 'One patient (13) had severe mental retardation and spasticity which were attributed to cerebral trauma'; it was attributed to patient 13 (the '12' read as a reference superscript). The age at death '5% years' is OCR-garbled, so deceased_age_iso8601 is null. The neuropathy list '(1, 2, 5, 7–10, 12, 13 and 15)' has a garbled lead-in; 'the other 9 patients' (the list minus 13) were read as having peripheral neuropathy. Contradictions: patient 5 'had no lymphadenopathy' on physical examination vs 'enlarged lymph nodes ... mesentric in 5' (both rows emitted; checklist lymphadenopathy not reported); patient 15 'No abnormalities of the peripheral nervous system were found' vs inclusion in the neuropathy list (both rows; checklist not reported; Discussion lists ocular movement disturbance among the manifestations). Patient 5's 'no ... cutaneous lesions or neurologic abnormalities' refers to the 1962 evaluation; skin lesions and neuropathy developed later, so these are recorded as time-limited exclusions, not contradictions. Group exclusions: skin deposits excluded for patients 6, 8, 9 (examined list '1–6, 8–10, 13 and 16' minus found list '1, 3, 4, 5, 10, 13 and 16'); jejunal foam cells excluded for patient 6 ('only patient 2 had foam cells in jejunum'). Low HDL marked observed only where stated for the person (2, 4, 5, parents of 13); for patients 15 and 16 and the father of patient 16 HDL values are printed without a statement that they are low, so left not reported. Patient 2's triglycerides 237 (mean normal 40) were not marked as hypertriglyceridemia (no explicit statement); low LDL marked from '44 (50–170)' with the stated normal range. Patient 4 'no hepatosplenomegaly' was not used to exclude hepatomegaly or splenomegaly separately; patient 16 'spleen also was palpable' recorded as a feature but checklist splenomegaly left not reported; normal neurologic/ophthalmologic examinations (patient 16) and normal hemogram (patient 15) exclude nothing more specific (D-27). Tonsillar remnants with typical enlargement/coloration (patients 4–8 and 10) counted as orange-colored or enlarged tonsils. Rectal plaque-like foam-cell lesions counted as intestinal mucosal lipid deposits; patient 2's jejunal foam cells are described as in the lamina propria of jejunal mucosa in the case report but in the submucosa in Results/Discussion.
